newsitem.title: USA: Cheney blasts U.S. Congress over use of sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Cheney blasts U.S. Congress over use of sanctions.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of Defense Dick Cheney, now chairman of a major oil services firm, blasted the U.S. Congress for its reliance on economic sanctions to carry out foreign policy.

In a speech to the Independent Petroleum Association of America conference on Friday, Cheney said stepped up oil production outside the Middle East has muted concerns about supply disruptions in the United States.
"Right now, I'm more concerned about the Congress of the United States doing something stupid for us than I am about instability overseas," said Cheney, chairman of Dallas-based Halliburton Corp.

The Washington, D.C.-based trade group estimated oil and products imports in 1997 will rise to 51.5 percent of domestic consumption, continuing a trend of increased reliance on foreign crude and refined products.

But with increasing supplies from countries like Venezuela and Nigeria, the threat of disruptions from the Middle East has been reduced. "We're in much better shape now than we were in that regard," he said.

Since joining the oil industry two years ago, Cheney has been an outspoken critic of Congressional efforts to impose sanctions in areas of the world where U.S. companies are exploring and producing oil and natural gas.
"What we see is this attitude in Congress that this is a cost-free sanction," he said.
